cards.text: Abraham's chief servant came looking for a wife for Isaac, Abraham's son (Genesis 24:2-4), and he's just met Rebekah, the young woman who watered his camels at the spring (Genesis 24:15-20). Now Rebekah RUNS home and tells her mother's household everything. That's no casual stroll, friend, that's the whole family group chat blowing up at once.
Rebekah has a brother named Laban. And Laban RUSHES out to the man at the spring.

cards.question: Laban sees new jewelry on his sister Rebekah: a ring and ___.

cards.text: As soon as Laban sees that jewelry and hears what Rebekah says, he's out the door, and he finds the man standing by the camels near the spring. Nobody moves that fast for me unless the oven timer goes off.

cards.question: Laban invites Abraham's servant to come inside. What does Laban call him?
Laban tells Abraham's servant he hasn't had time to get anything ready for him or his camels.

cards.text: So the man comes to the house, the camels get unloaded and fed, and there's water to wash his feet and his companions' feet. Then a meal is set in front of him, and friend, after a trip like that, I'd be face-first in it before anybody said grace.

cards.question: With the meal in front of him, Abraham's servant eats first and saves the talking for later.

cards.text: Laban says, “Please speak.” So the man tells them he's Abraham's servant, and that the LORD has greatly blessed Abraham with sheep and cattle, silver and gold, servants, camels and donkeys.

cards.question: Abraham's servant says Abraham's wife had a son in her old age. What has Abraham given that son?

cards.text: Then the servant tells them about an oath Abraham made him swear. Isaac's wife can't come from the daughters of the Canaanites, the people whose land Abraham lives in.

cards.question: Abraham's oath ruled out the daughters of the Canaanites. So where did Abraham send his servant to find a wife for Isaac instead?

answers.text: To his father's house and family
To the great cities of Egypt
To the towns along the Jordan

cards.text: The servant says he asked Abraham, “What if the woman will not come back with me?” And Abraham told him the LORD would send His angel with him and make his journey a success.

cards.question: Abraham told his servant that if the family refused to give her, the servant would be released from the oath.

cards.text: Then the servant walks them through his day at the spring: his prayer, and Rebekah showing up before he'd even finished praying, offering to water his camels too. Ask me how MY day went and you get the whole batch, crumbs and all, so I respect this man.

cards.question: Abraham's servant says that before he put the ring and bracelets on Rebekah, he asked her something. What did he ask?

cards.text: Then, he says, he bowed down and worshiped the LORD, who led him on the right road to the granddaughter of Abraham's brother.

cards.question: Abraham's servant finishes by asking the family for their answer. If they say no, what will he do?

cards.text: Abraham's servant has told the whole story and asked for an answer. Now Laban and Bethuel, Rebekah's father, speak up, and I'm sitting here holding my breath like it's the last batch in the oven.

cards.question: Laban and Bethuel answer Abraham's servant. Who do they say all this is from?

cards.text: They tell him, “Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go…” Abraham's servant hears that and bows down to the ground before the LORD, and I love this man for it.

cards.question: Abraham's servant brings out jewels of silver and gold and clothing, and he gives them to Rebekah.

cards.text: Abraham's servant gives precious gifts to her brother and her mother too. Then he and the men with him eat, drink and spend the night.

cards.question: The next morning, Abraham's servant says, “Send me on my way to my master.” What do Rebekah's brother and mother ask for?

answers.text: A little more time with her

cards.question: Abraham's servant agrees to wait before he leaves.

cards.text: The servant says, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success.” So her family says they'll call the girl and ask her opinion.

cards.question: They call Rebekah and ask her, “Will you go with this man?” What does she say?

cards.text: Three words, and I take longer than that to pick a topping. So they send their sister Rebekah on her way with her nurse, Abraham's servant and his men.

cards.question: Before Rebekah leaves, her family blesses her. What do they wish for her?

answers.text: To be the mother of thousands
To come back home again soon
To be rich in land and gold

cards.text: And the blessing keeps going: “May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.” Friend, that's not a send-off, that's a whole PARADE.

cards.question: Rebekah sets out on the camels along with her servant girls.

cards.text: Now Isaac has just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he's living in the Negev. Early in the evening, he goes out to the field to meditate.

cards.question: Isaac is out in the field early in the evening. When he looks up, what does he see coming?

cards.text: Rebekah looks up and sees Isaac, and she gets down off her camel. Friend, THIS is the slow-motion part of the movie.

cards.question: Rebekah asks Abraham's servant who the man in the field is. When he answers, “It is my master,” she takes her ___ and covers herself.

cards.text: Then the servant tells Isaac all that he had done. If it's anything like the version he gave at Laban's house, Isaac better pull up a chair.

cards.question: Isaac brings Rebekah into the tent of his mother ___.

cards.text: Isaac takes Rebekah as his wife, he loves her, and he's comforted after his mother's death. But Abraham's story isn't finished yet, friend.
